findings.description:
FIND — scan_health() misreports missing tools as available. In bench/endocrine.py, each runner returns `[]` when `_run_tool()` reports `stderr == "NOT_FOUND"`, and scan_health() then sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` unconditionally unless an exception was raised. Evidence: run_pyright/run_ruff/run_bandit/run_mypy all convert NOT_FOUND into empty diagnostics instead of surfacing unavailability, and scan_health has no other availability check.
FOLLOW: This creates a fail-open health scan: the endocrine layer can report a clean scan with zero diagnostics while all analyzers are absent. insect_brain consumes health_scan as a structured health signal for round decisions; zero diagnostics from “available” tools is materially different from “tool unavailable”. It also corrupts reviewer-facing telemetry and can hide infrastructure regressions in the PoC happy path, since the whole health monitor appears to function while doing nothing.
findings.proposed_fix: FIX — propagate tool availability explicitly from each runner or from _run_tool returncode/stderr, and in scan_health mark a tool unavailable when invocation returned NOT_FOUND or TIMEOUT instead of treating empty diagnostics as success.

findings.description:
FIND — health_trend() produces ragged time series that omit zero-count rounds for categories absent in a scan. It appends counts only for categories present in each scan’s `counts_by_category`; categories missing in a round get no entry. After scans like `{security: 1}` then `{style: 1}`, the returned trend is `{"security": [1], "style": [1]}` instead of aligned per-round series like `{"security": [1,0], "style": [0,1]}`.
FOLLOW: Any consumer comparing category trends across rounds receives malformed history and can misread disappearance as missing data rather than zero. Since this method exists specifically “for the insect brain to detect worsening/improving code health,” ragged vectors make trend analysis and thresholding unreliable.
findings.proposed_fix: FIX — build the union of categories across scan history and emit one count per round per category, inserting 0 when a category is absent in a given scan.

findings.description:
FIND — the advertised defect-detection capability is partially dead code. endocrine.py declares DefectCategory.OFF_BY_ONE and RACE_CONDITION, and the module docstring claims defect classification for “off-by-one” and “race conditions,” but no categoriser path in run_pyright/run_ruff/run_bandit/run_mypy ever emits either category. All pyright/mypy diagnostics collapse to TYPE_SAFETY or NULL_DEREF; ruff mostly maps to DEAD_CODE/STYLE/SECURITY.
FOLLOW: Downstream, counts_by_category and any reviewer relying on endocrine defect categories will never see those categories fire, so the feature does not deliver the claimed coverage. In a PoC this is medium severity rather than critical, but it is still misleading telemetry and effectively dead functionality.
findings.proposed_fix: FIX — either add minimal pattern-based mappings that can actually emit OFF_BY_ONE and RACE_CONDITION from tool messages, or remove those categories from the advertised capability until supported. The simpler sufficient fix is to stop advertising unsupported categories.

findings.description:
FIND — `scan_health()` marks tools as available whenever the runner function returns normally, even when the binary is missing or timed out. Evidence: `run_pyright()`, `run_ruff()`, `run_bandit()`, and `run_mypy()` all return `[]` on `_run_tool(...).stderr == "NOT_FOUND"`; `scan_health()` then sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` unconditionally after `diags = runner(existing)`. The same false-positive availability occurs on timeout because `_run_tool()` returns a synthetic `CompletedProcess(..., returncode=-1, stderr="TIMEOUT")`, but the runners mostly just parse empty stdout and return `[]`.
FOLLOW: The endocrine layer’s primary contract is to tell the insect brain whether health tooling actually ran. With the current logic, missing/broken analyzers are reported as healthy zero-diagnostic runs. That silently degrades the “health scan” feature into dead infrastructure: reviewers see no diagnostics and no unavailable-tool signal, the insect brain cannot distinguish clean code from non-executed tools, and fix evaluation baselines that reuse these runners can also undercount issues without surfacing that the checker never ran.
findings.proposed_fix: FIX — make each runner return both diagnostics and an execution-status flag, or more simply have `_run_tool()` status checked in each runner and raise/propagate a sentinel on `NOT_FOUND`/`TIMEOUT`; then set `tools_available[tool_name] = False` in `scan_health()` for those cases instead of treating empty diagnostics as success.

findings.description:
FIND — the advertised defect-detection capability is only partially implemented and some declared features never fire. `DefectCategory` includes `OFF_BY_ONE` and `RACE_CONDITION`, and the module docstring promises classification for “off-by-one, race conditions”, but no categoriser path in `_categorise_pyright`, `_categorise_ruff`, `run_bandit`, or `run_mypy` ever emits those categories. `run_crosshair` is also absent despite `CROSSHAIR_BIN` and the top-level docs listing CrossHair.
FOLLOW: This creates dead feature claims in the endocrine interface. The insect brain and human reviewers may assume endocrine is monitoring those defect classes when it never can. At PoC stage that is a misleading-output problem: the feature appears present by API/docs/constants but cannot trigger, reducing trust in the health report and making debugging harder when expected categories stay permanently zero.
findings.proposed_fix: FIX — remove unimplemented categories/tool claims from the endocrine interface for now, or wire the simplest real implementation: add a `run_crosshair()` path and only keep categories that current tool parsers can actually emit.

findings.description:
FIND — `health_trend()` returns ragged per-category histories and omits zero counts for rounds where a category did not appear. Evidence: it iterates `for scan in self._scan_history: for cat, count in scan.counts_by_category.items(): trend.setdefault(cat, []).append(count)`. If a category is absent in a round, no `0` is appended, so list positions no longer align to round indices.
FOLLOW: Any consumer comparing round-over-round trends can misread category trajectories because list index is not stable across rounds. A category sequence like `[5, 1]` may mean rounds 0 and 2, not consecutive rounds. That makes worsening/improving-health logic unreliable and can mis-trigger or miss pacing or human review decisions based on trends.
findings.proposed_fix: FIX — build trends over all known categories across all scans and append `scan.counts_by_category.get(cat, 0)` for every round so each category history has one entry per scan.

findings.description:
FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` claims `context_budget: int` but contains runtime handling for `dict`, then immediately compares `if context_budget > 0:` and divides by it. This is an interface mismatch with the function signature and datamodel. The defensive dict branch implies callers may pass per-model budgets, but the function collapses them to `max(...)`, which understates pressure for smaller-budget models.
FOLLOW: Downstream pacing decisions can be silently wrong in multi-model runs with budget overrides: the endocrine signal may report context as healthy because it uses the largest budget, while one or more models are already near exhaustion. That weakens the insect brain’s degrade/relay decisions and makes the signal misleading.
findings.proposed_fix: FIX — make the interface honest: accept only an integer budget in this function and remove the dict branch; callers should pass the actual effective budget they want evaluated.

findings.description:
FIND — slow-model and response-size “median” calculations use `sorted(values)[len(values)//2]`, which is not the statistical median for even-sized sets. With 4 or 6 models this selects the upper middle value rather than the average of the two middles. In a 5-model system this is usually fine, but the code is generic and the endocrine layer is infrastructure.
FOLLOW: Threshold-based pacing signals can shift materially around the trigger boundary, especially with an even number of active models after failures. That can suppress legitimate slow-model/context-growth signals or emit spurious ones, affecting relay degradation and timeout adjustments.
findings.proposed_fix: FIX — use `statistics.median()` for durations and response sizes.

findings.description:
FIND — `compute_pacing_signals` novelty plateau detection requires `len(novelty_counts) >= 3 and round_idx >= 2`, then checks `novelty_counts[-3:]`. But `novelty_counts` is passed from the caller as a list where index = round number. If rounds are skipped or the list is shorter than `round_idx`, the check `round_idx >= 2` is redundant with `len(novelty_counts) >= 3`, but more importantly: the condition `all(n <= 1 for n in recent)` triggers on 3 consecutive rounds with ≤1 novel findings. At round 2 (the third round, 0-indexed), with `novelty_counts = [5, 1, 0]`, the plateau fires immediately. Three rounds is very early to declare convergence plateau — this threshold is too aggressive for the typical 6-8 round experiment.

FOLLOW: An overly aggressive novelty plateau signal causes the insect brain to consider convergence too early. If the brain acts on `check_convergence` using this signal, experiments may terminate prematurely before models have fully explored the search space. The signal itself doesn't force termination (it's advisory via `suggested_action="check_convergence"`), so the downstream impact depends on how the insect brain consumes it. Given PoC context, this is MEDIUM — the signal fires too early but doesn't directly break operation.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the window from 3 to 4 rounds and require `round_idx >= 3`: `if len(novelty_counts) >= 4 and round_idx >= 3:` with `recent = novelty_counts[-4:]` and `if all(n <= 1 for n in recent):`. This gives models one more round to recover before plateau is signalled.

findings.description:
FIND — `EndocrineLayer` has a `health_trend()` method that returns diagnostic count trends across rounds, but it is never called by any code path in the codebase. The insect brain's interface (`insect_brain.py`) does not reference `health_trend()`, and the `EndocrineReport` dataclass doesn't include trend data. The `_scan_history` list grows unboundedly across rounds with no consumer.

FOLLOW: This is dead code that never fires. The health trend feature is documented as "for the insect brain to detect worsening/improving code health" but the insect brain doesn't consume it. No downstream consequence beyond memory growth from accumulating `HealthScan` objects in `_scan_history`. At PoC scale (6-8 rounds), memory is not a concern.
findings.proposed_fix: No fix needed for PoC — this is LOW/documentation-level. If trend detection is wanted, the insect brain needs to call `endo.health_trend()` and use the result.

findings.description:
FIND — `compute_pacing_signals` receives `context_budget` which may be a dict (per-model budgets). The defensive check `if isinstance(context_budget, dict): context_budget = max(context_budget.values())` extracts the max value. But `cumulative_context_chars` is a single integer representing total chars across all models. Comparing total cumulative chars against a single model's budget is semantically wrong — `context_fraction` will be inflated by the number of models. With 5 models each at 80K budget, cumulative chars of 200K gives `context_fraction = 200000/80000 = 2.5`, triggering the 0.8 threshold when no individual model is anywhere near budget.

FOLLOW: The context_growth pacing signal fires prematurely and persistently once cumulative chars exceed 80% of one model's budget. Since cumulative chars grow roughly linearly with models × rounds, this signal fires after ~1-2 rounds in a 5-model experiment and never stops firing. The insect brain receives `suggested_action="degrade_relay"` every round from early on, which may cause unnecessary context degradation.

FIND — `compute_pacing_signals` slow model detection uses integer division for median: `sorted(durations)[len(durations) // 2]`. With an even number of models (e.g., 4), this picks the element at index 2 (the third-smallest), not the true median (average of elements at indices 1 and 2). The threshold is then `median * 2.5`, which is slightly higher than it should be, making slow model detection marginally less sensitive.

FOLLOW: Minor — the median is off by one rank position for even-length lists. With typical model timings, the practical difference is small. The `> 30.0` second absolute floor provides a safety net. This is not worth fixing at PoC stage.
findings.proposed_fix: No fix needed for PoC. If precision matters: `median_duration = sorted(durations)[len(durations) // 2]` is adequate for odd-length lists and a reasonable approximation for even-length.

findings.description:
FIND — `scan_health` runs pyright, ruff, bandit, and mypy sequentially on every source file between every round. For a multi-file project, this is 4 subprocess invocations per scan. The comment says "they're fast enough on a single file set" but pyright in particular can take 5-15 seconds on first invocation (type inference cache cold start). With 6-8 rounds, that's 4-8 minutes spent on health scans alone.

FOLLOW: Performance impact only — does not affect correctness. At PoC scale with 2-3 source files, this is acceptable. The `_TOOL_TIMEOUT = 60` prevents hangs.
